title: Fix prior cache isolation across account switches
body: ## Bug and impact - Starting-load and LiftState prior caches were stored in device-global UserDefaults and were not cleared on sign-out, account deletion, or account switches. - A shared device could let User B inherit User A's learned priors, causing incorrect cold-start load/LiftState seeding and an account-isolation leak. - Prior RPC HTTP/config failures were also treated as empty successful payloads, allowing transient failures to wipe valid cached priors. ## Root cause - The new prior sync services used a process-wide 12h rate limit and global cache keys without an auth-boundary reset. - HTTP >=400/config-disabled paths returned `[]`, which flowed into `replace(with:)` as an intentional empty cache. ## Fix - Added account-boundary reset/in-flight invalidation for both prior sync services. - Wired resets into account switch isolation, sign-out, and account deletion wipes. - Changed prior RPC failure paths to throw so valid caches are preserved after transient errors. - Added MultiAccountFlow regression coverage to assert prior caches do not bleed across account switches. - Updated `TASKS.md` checklist and notes. ## Validation - `git diff --check` passed. - Focused iOS test commands were attempted but skipped in this Linux environment because `xcodebuild` and `swift` are not installed.
